rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since spatial nearness is impossible here, the nearness is temporal: the time of people’s reckoning has approached.
rows.anchor: القرب لا يعقل إلا في المكان والزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer to the apparent delay is that the reckoning is near in God’s measure, as 22:47 says a day with God is like a thousand years.
rows.anchor: أنه مقترب عند الله تعالى والدليل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer is that every event still to come is near however long its wait; only what has passed is distant, as the cited verse says.
rows.anchor: وإنما البعيد هو الذي انقرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A deadline is called near once more time has elapsed than remains; by that measure the Hour is near because less of the period of obligation remains than has passed.
rows.anchor: إذا كان الماضي أكثر من الباقي

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet compared his mission and the Hour to two fingers as evidence of their closeness.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام : ( بعثت أنا والساعة كهاتين )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text reports the claim that the Prophet sealed prophethood because less of the period of religious obligation remained than had elapsed.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه قيل إنه عليه السلام ختم به النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the Hour’s nearness benefits those bound by the law by moving them to repent and free themselves from sins.
rows.anchor: إنما ذكر تعالى هذا الاقتراب لما فيه من المصلحة للمكلفين فيكون أقرب إلى تلافي الذنوب والتحرر عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time is left unspecified because concealment is more beneficial, just as concealing the time of death is.
rows.anchor: إنما لم يعين الوقت لأجل أن كتمانه أصلح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Resurrection the Day of Reckoning emphasizes that accounting exposes a person’s state and makes the warning more frightening.
rows.anchor: الفائدة في تسمية يوم القيامة بيوم الحساب أن الحساب هو الكاشف عن حال المرء فالخوف من ذكره أعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People here means those who are subject to reckoning, the morally responsible, rather than those with no part in it.
rows.anchor: يجب أن يكون المراد بالناس من له مدخل في الحساب وهم المكلفون دون من لا مدخل له

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the people as the polytheists; the generic term denotes only part of its class because the following description concerns polytheists.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : المراد بالناس المشركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their heedlessness is failure to remember or consider the reckoning and their fate, despite reason requiring recompense for good and evil.
rows.anchor: غافلون عن حسابهم ساهون لا يتفكرون في عاقبتهم مع اقتضاء عقولهم أنه لا بد من جزاء المحسن والمسيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When signs and warnings awaken them from heedlessness, they turn away and block their ears.
rows.anchor: إذا انتبهوا من سنة الغفلة ورقدة الجهالة مما يتلى عليهم من الآيات والنذر أعرضوا وسدوا أسماعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They kept their private talk secret partly because conspirators customarily hide consultations from their enemies while seeking a way to undermine the Prophet’s mission.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه كان ذلك شبهة التشاور فيما بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may also have hidden their conversation so they could challenge the Prophet and believers to reveal what they had said.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يسروا نجواهم بذلك ثم يقولوا لرسول الله والمؤمنين إن كان ما تدعونه حقا فأخبرونا بما أسررناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their two attacks on prophethood were that Muhammad was a human like them and that his message was sorcery; al-Rāzī rejects both.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه بشر مثلهم . والثاني : أن الذي أتى به سحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophethood is established by miracles and proofs, not by outward form; a human messenger is especially apt for humans to accept and feel at ease with.
rows.anchor: لأن النبوة تقف صحتها على المعجزات والدلائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the message sorcery is ignorant: the Prophet’s Quran and other signs were manifest, without trickery or deception.
rows.anchor: لأن كل ما أتى به الرسول من القرآن وغيره ظاهر الحال لا تمويه فيه ولا تلبيس فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran’s repeated challenge to eloquent opponents, who were strongly motivated to answer it and faced no obstacle, proves their inability to match it and its miraculous character.
rows.anchor: وكانوا في نهاية الحرص على إبطال أمره وأقوى الأمور في إبطال أمره معارضة القرآن فلو قدروا على المعارضة لامتنع أن لا يأتوا بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their failure to answer shows they recognized the truth, while they used this false accusation to mislead weaker followers despite their own stubborn denial.
rows.anchor: فلما لم يأتوا بها دلنا ذلك على أنه في نفسه معجزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After proving God transcendent of partner, opposite, and rival, the passage also refutes the claim that He has a child.
rows.anchor: لما بين بالدلائل الباهرة كونه منزها عن الشريك والضد والند أردف ذلك ببراءته عن اتخاذ الولد

rows.speaker: خزاعة
rows.claim: The verse was revealed concerning Khuzāʿa, who called the angels God’s daughters and claimed God was related by marriage to the jinn, as 37:158 recounts.
rows.anchor: نزلت في خزاعة حيث قالوا : الملائكة بنات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A child would resemble its parent in one respect and differ in another; that entails composition in God, and every composite is possible rather than necessary, incompatible with divinity.
rows.anchor: وما به المشاركة غير ما به الممايزة فيقع التركيب في ذات الله سبحانه وتعالى وكل مركب ممكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels are servants, which contradicts filiation, though they are honored and preferred over other servants.
rows.anchor: أخبر عنهم بأنهم عباد والعبودية تنافي الولادة إلا أنهم مكرمون مفضلون على سائر العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading joins مُكْرَمُونَ to لا يسبقونه; the phrase means the angels follow God’s speech and do not speak before Him, and their deeds likewise await His command.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : { مكرمون * لا يسبقونه } من سابقته فسبقته أسبقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing that God knows all things, including their outward and inward states, leads the angels to complete humility and servitude.
rows.anchor: لما علموا كونه سبحانه عالما بجميع المعلومات علموا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains what is before and behind them as the deeds they have already done and those they will do.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يعلم ما قدموا وما أخروا من أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported explanation takes what is before them as the afterlife and what is behind them as the world; another reverses the two.
rows.anchor: ما بين أيديهم الآخرة وما خلفهم الدنيا وقيل على عكس ذلك

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says God knows what occurred before creating the angels and what will occur after their creation.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : يعلم ما كان قبل أن يخلقهم وما يكون بعد خلقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In reality, the angels remain within God’s dominion and under His power; they therefore cannot merit worship or intercede for anyone without His permission.
rows.anchor: يتقلبون تحت قدرته في ملكوته وهو محيط بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels intercede only for someone whom God approves.
rows.anchor: ثم كشف عن هذا المعنى فقال : { ولا يشفعون إلا لمن ارتضى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In مشفقون من خشيته, the verbal noun is annexed to its object; the angels fear God and do not feel secure from His requital.
rows.anchor: فأضيف المصدر إلى المفعول ومشفقون خائفون ولا يأمنون مكره

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet saw Gabriel on the Night Journey collapsed like a saddle cloth from fear of God; al-Rāzī gives no grading.
rows.anchor: وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( أنه رأى جبريل عليه السلام ليلة المعراج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that none speaks except by permission of the Merciful is offered as a parallel, cited here as 4:38.
rows.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى : { لا يتكلمون إلا من أذن له الرحمان }

words: وَحَرَامٌ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَٰهَآ أَنَّهُمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poem uses حرام to mean obligatory; naming one opposite by the other is a familiar metaphor, as 42:40 also does.
rows.anchor: وأما الاستعمال فلأن تسمية أحد الضدين باسم الآخر مجاز مشهور

rows.speaker: مجاهد والحسن
rows.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan take لا يرجعون to mean that the people do not turn back from polytheism.
rows.anchor: لا يرجعون عن الشرك ولا يتولون عنه وهو قول مجاهد والحسن

rows.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
rows.claim: Qatāda and Muqātil understand the phrase as saying that the dead do not return to this world.
rows.anchor: لا يرجعون إلى الدنيا وهو قول قتادة ومقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative keeps حرام in its literal sense and treats لا as extra, yielding a prohibition on a destroyed town’s return to this world, as in 36:50.
rows.anchor: يجعل في قوله : { لا يرجعون } صلة زائدة كما أنه صلة

rows.speaker: طائفة من المفسرين
rows.claim: A group of commentators retains the literal sense of حرام and takes the phrase to mean the people are barred from turning away from polytheism and abandoning faith.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول طائفة من المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If حرام predicates something else, the implied object can be the preceding righteous work and its appreciated reward; their failure to leave unbelief explains why that is withheld.
rows.anchor: فالتقدير وحرام على قرية أهلكناها ذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With this last construction, either إنهم with kasra or أنهم with fatḥa can carry the explanation that they do not turn back from unbelief.
rows.anchor: هذا على قراءة إنهم بالكسر والقراءة بالفتح يصح حملها أيضا على هذا أي أنهم لا يرجعون

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: On Abū Muslim’s reading, their return to the afterlife is obligatory and reaches its limit when Gog and Magog are released and the Hour approaches, making the unbelievers among the first at the Resurrection gathering.
rows.anchor: على تأويل أبي مسلم فالمعنى أن رجوعهم إلى الآخرة واجب حتى أن وجوبه يبلغ إلى حيث أنه إذا فتحت يأجوج ومأجوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Abū Muslim’s reading, حتى attaches to حرام as an endpoint of the same kind; the quoted conditional and its Resurrection-day result are separated in time, but the small gap counts as nothing.
rows.anchor: فحتى متعلقة بحرام وهي غاية له ولكنه غاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under the other interpretations, their inability to return remains in force until the Hour is established.
rows.anchor: وأما على التأويلات الباقية فالمعنى أن امتناع رجوعهم لا يزول حتى تقوم الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction means the barrier of Gog and Magog was opened, with the noun barrier omitted; feminine فتحت follows the omitted feminine noun. Another view supplies “the region of Gog.”
rows.anchor: المعنى فتح سد يأجوج ومأجوج فحذف المضاف وأدخلت علامة التأنيث في فتحت لما حذف المضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gog and Magog are two tribes of humankind; it is said they make up nine tenths of all people and emerge when the barrier opens.
rows.anchor: هما قبيلتان من جنس الإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says God opens the barrier directly; another says it opens when God makes the earth level and its solid parts lose their firmness.
rows.anchor: قيل : السد يفتحه الله تعالى ابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about their rushing is parenthetical; the main sequence is Gog and Magog being released, the true promise nearing, and the unbelievers’ eyes staring.
rows.anchor: فحشو في أثناء الكلام ، والمعنى إذا فتحت يأجوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حدب is a raised place or mound, hence the expressions for a hump of earth and a hump on the back.
rows.anchor: والحدب النشز من الأرض ، ومنه حدبة الأرض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads the phrase in light of the dead rushing from the graves in 36:51.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with ḍamma on the sīn is noted; the verbs nasala and ʿasala mean to hurry.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بضم السين ونسل وعسل أسرع

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators say those rushing are Gog and Magog.
rows.anchor: قال أكثر المفسرين إنه كناية عن يأجوج ومأجوج

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says all morally responsible people emerge from their graves from every place and are gathered at the reckoning.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : هو كناية عن جميع المكلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers the Gog and Magog referent because it preserves the passage’s sequence; their reported immense numbers also explain their approach from every rise.
rows.anchor: والأول هو الأوجه وإلا لتفكك النظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The true promise that has approached is unquestionably the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: لا شبهة أن الوعد المذكور هو يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here إذا marks suddenness; وعد is a figurative name for the appointed event, and إذا can stand in the result for the fā, as in 30:36.
rows.anchor: فاعلم أن إذا ههنا للمفاجأة فسمى الموعد وعدا تجوزا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fā can accompany إذا and reinforce the connection between condition and result; either فإذا هي شاخصة or فهي شاخصة is sound.
rows.anchor: فإذا جاءت الفاء معها تعاونتا على وصل الجزاء بالشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One grammatical analysis makes هي refer to the eyes, first referring to them implicitly and then naming them explicitly.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أن تكون كناية عن الأبصار ، والمعنى فإذا أبصار الذين كفروا شاخصة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats هي as an ʿimād pronoun, replaceable by masculine هو; feminine agreement suits الأبصار, while masculine suits the ʿimād construction.
rows.anchor: وجاز التأنيث لأن الأبصار مؤنثة وجاز التذكير للعماد وهو قول الفراء

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh takes هي to refer to the story or event: the event is that the unbelievers’ eyes stare fixedly then.
rows.anchor: وقال سيبويه الضمير للقصة بمعنى فإذا القصة شاخصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Resurrection the unbelievers’ eyes stare without nearly blinking, from the day’s horrors and fear of what awaits them.
rows.anchor: أن القيامة إذا قامت شخصت أبصار هؤلاء من شدة الأهوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted يقولون is understood before يا ويلنا: they say, “Woe to us.”
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه لا بد قبل قوله يا ويلنا من حذف والتقدير يقولون يا ويلنا

words: قَدْ كُنَّا فِى غَفْلَةٍۢ مِّنْ هَٰذَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They admit that in worldly life they were heedless of this, denying that it would happen.
rows.anchor: يعني في الدنيا حيث كذبناه وقلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They confess that their heedlessness and denial of Muhammad, along with worship of idols, wronged themselves.
rows.anchor: بل كنا ظالمين أنفسنا بتلك الغفلة وبتكذيب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وعبادة الأوثان

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan vocalizes البعث with moving vowels, comparing it to الحلب and الطرد.
rows.anchor: قرأ الحسن { من البعث } بالتحريك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: One reading puts kasra on the tāʾ and rāʾ of مخلقة وغير مخلقة; Ibn Abī ʿAblah reads both in the accusative.
rows.anchor: { مخلقة وغير مخلقة } بجر التاء والراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The familiar recitation uses nūn in لنبين, ونقر, and نخرجكم; Ibn Abī ʿAblah uses yāʾ in all three.
rows.anchor: القراءة المعروفة بالنون في قوله : { لنبين } وفي قوله

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Al-Sīrāfī reports from Dāwūd, from Yaʿqūb, ونقر with fatḥa on nūn and ḍamma on qāf and rāʾ, from قرّ الماء, “he poured the water”; another report has rāʾ in the accusative.
rows.anchor: روى السيرافي عن داود عن يعقوب ونقر بفتح النون وضم القاف والراء وهو من قر الماء إذا صبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other nūn readings put ونقر and نخرجكم in the accusative.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : ونقر ونخرجكم بنصب الراء والجيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ readings include يقر ويخرجكم with fatḥa on qāf, rāʾ, and jīm; another has ḍamma on those vowels; a third has fatḥa on yāʾ, kasra on qāf, and ḍamma on rāʾ.
rows.anchor: يقر ويخرجكم بفتح القاف والراء والجيم

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abū Ḥātim reads يُتوفّى with fatḥa on yāʾ, making God the one who takes the person.
rows.anchor: أبو حاتم { ومنكم من يتوفى } بفتح الياء

rows.speaker: ابن عمرة والأعمش
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmara and al-Aʿmash read العمر with a still mīm.
rows.anchor: ابن عمرة والأعمش { العمر } بإسكان الميم

rows.speaker: عبدالله
rows.claim: In ʿAbd Allāh’s codex the wording is ومنكم من يتوفى ومنكم من يكون شيوخا instead of the familiar reading.
rows.anchor: وفي حرف عبدالله ومنكم من يتوفى ومنكم من يكون شيوخا بغير القراءة المعروفة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads وربأت, meaning it rose; al-ʿUmari reports this from him with the hamza softened.
rows.anchor: وربت أبو جعفر وربأت أي ارتفعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The segment also notes the reading وأنه باعث without naming its reader.
rows.anchor: وقرىء وأنه باعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Answering those who dispute resurrection without knowledge, God argues from two signs: the initial creation of humans and the revival of plants; human creation follows the argument in 36:79 and 17:51.
rows.anchor: الدلالة على صحة ذلك من وجهين : أحدهما : الاستدلال بخلقة الحيوان أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that humanity’s ancestor Adam was created from dust, as 3:59 and 20:55 say.
rows.anchor: إنا خلقنا أصلكم وهو آدم عليه السلام من تراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, human semen and menstrual blood come from nourishment; animal nourishment ultimately traces to plants, and plants to earth and water, so humans are from dust.
rows.anchor: وهما إنما يتولدان من الأغذية ، والأغذية إما حيوان أو نبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuṭfa means a small amount of any liquid; here it means male semen, showing God’s transformation of dry dust into a subtle fluid with no resemblance to it.
rows.anchor: والنطفة اسم للماء القليل أي ماء كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlaqa is a clotted piece of blood, sharply different from the liquid that preceded it.
rows.anchor: العلقة قطعة الدم الجامدة ، ولا شك أن بين الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A muḍgha is a small piece of flesh, roughly the amount one chews.
rows.anchor: فالمضغة اللحمة الصغيرة قدر ما يمضغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukhallaqa means smoothed, even, and free of defect; Arabic uses خلق for smoothing a tooth-stick or rod and calls a smooth rock خلقاء.
rows.anchor: والمخلقة المسواة الملساء السالمة من النقصان والعيب

rows.speaker: قتادة والضحاك
rows.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the formed and unformed are embryos with complete or incomplete form, senses, and features; their difference explains variation in people’s bodies and appearance.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد من تمت فيه أحوال الخلق ومن لم تتم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid identifies the formed with a child born alive and the unformed with a miscarriage.
rows.anchor: المخلقة الولد الذي يخرج حيا وغير المخلقة السقط وهو قول مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view calls the formed one shaped and the unformed one an unshaped lump of flesh.
rows.anchor: المخلقة المصورة وغير المخلقة أي غير المصورة وهو الذي يبقى لحما من غير تخطيط وتشكيل

rows.speaker: عبدالله
rows.claim: Alqama reports from ʿAbd Allāh that an angel asks whether the embryo is formed; if not, the womb expels it as blood, while a formed embryo’s sex, provision, lifespan, and fate are copied from the Mother Book and accompany it through its remaining stages.
rows.anchor: عن عبدالله قال : ( إذا وقعت النطفة في الرحم

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffāl derives the terms from successive creation through stages: what has completed those successive formations is formed, and what has not is unformed.
rows.anchor: قال القفال : التخليق مأخوذ من الخلق فما تتابع عليه الأطوار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers the complete and incomplete human-form explanation because the verse addresses people who will become human; miscarriage is a less fitting referent where formation may never be complete.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول أقرب لأنه تعالى قال في أول الآية : { فإنا خلقناكم } وأشار إلى الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that some are not retained in the womb does not defeat his preferred view: an embryo may have complete or incomplete form and still be either retained or miscarried.
rows.anchor: فلنا إن ذلك لا يمنع من صحة ما ذكرنا في كون المضغة مخلقة وغير مخلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that God shows His free choice by making some embryos fully formed and others incomplete.
rows.anchor: لنبين لكم أن تغيير المضغة إلى المخلقة هو باختيار الفاعل المختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the account of human origins removes doubt about resurrection: one able to create these stages can restore the dead.
rows.anchor: إن كنتم في ريب من البعث فإنا أخبرناكم أنا خلقناكم من كذا وكذا لنبين لكم ما يزيل عنكم ذلك الريب

words: وَنُقِرُّ فِى ٱلْأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ مُّسَمًّۭى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God retains in the womb those He brings to birth; the appointed term is the time of delivery, which may be six months, nine months, four years, or as God decrees.
rows.anchor: من يبلغه الله تعالى حد الولادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طفلا is singular because it denotes the generic class; alternatively, each person is brought out as an infant, like the singular of the angels in 66:4.
rows.anchor: وإنما وحد الطفل لأن الغرض الدلالة على الجنس ويحتمل أن يخرج كل واحد منكم طفلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashudd means full strength, intellect, and discernment; it is a plural-form noun with no used singular, perhaps because strength involves multiple capacities.
rows.anchor: والأشد كمال القوة والعقل والتمييز وهو من ألفاظ الجموع التي لم يستعمل لها واحد وكأنها شدة في غير شيء واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God eases nurture and food so people pass through the stages between birth and maturity; an alternative says there is no intervening stage before the onset of full strength, so someone may remain an infant by age.
rows.anchor: ثم سهل في تربيتكم وأغذيتكم أمورا لتبلغوا أشدكم فنبه بذلك على الأحوال التي بين خروج الطفل من بطن أمه وبين بلوغ الأشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some people die while still at their full strength and maturity.
rows.anchor: أن منكم من يتوفى على قوته وكماله

words: وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others return to senility and dementia, becoming physically weak, dull in mind, and slow to understand like infants.
rows.anchor: إلى أرذل العمر وهو الهرم والخرف

words: لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍ شَيْـًۭٔا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although an infant knows some things, the negation is emphatic: the old person’s reason disappears, making it as though he knows nothing.
rows.anchor: قلنا المراد أنه يزول عقله فيصير كأنه لا يعلم شيئا لأن مثل ذلك قد يذكر في النفي لأجل المبالغة

words: وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects the claim that believers do not reach senility based on 95:5–6: being returned to the lowest state is blame or punishment, and the believers’ exception promises lasting reward.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من قال هذه الحالة لا تحصل للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second proof of resurrection is plant life: just as God first creates animals, He revives dead earth with rain.
rows.anchor: الوجه الثاني : الاستدلال بحال خلقة النبات على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamidah describes earth that is dry and without vegetation or green growth.
rows.anchor: وهمودها يبسها وخلوها عن النبات والخضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When rain falls, the land moves and swells with plants; اهتزت suggests joyful movement and is normally used for a good or beneficial event.
rows.anchor: والاهتزاز الحركة على سرور فلا يكاد يقال اهتز فلان لكيت وكيت إلا إذا كان الأمر من المحاسن والمنافع
